title: The Bedrock Literacy Vault

features.name: the-stone-that-reads-itself
features.desc-on-touch: Bedrock carved with languages older than plants. The stone is learning to read its own surface, tracing letters that were never written.

features.name: the-root-alphabet-where-first-names-begin
features.desc-on-touch: Roots have written their first names in the bedrock. Each letter is a root that learned to read before it learned to grow.

features.name: the-literate-dark-that-teaches-itself-language
features.desc-on-touch: The darkness learns to speak in every language roots remember from before planting. The soil becomes a text.

features.name: the-bedrock-memory-chamber
features.desc-on-touch: You remember being rooted, being deep, being the first syllable of your own name. The bedrock remembers you too.

reverie.title: REVERIE — red earth at night, names learning to root
narr: You lie beneath the tree where Leif placed his hand.
The soil is warm. He is reading the root-script aloud,
names that came before names, learnings in the dark.
"What were they called before we found them?" you ask.
"They called themselves," he says. "We are only listening late."
The earth holds two of you, reading the same word two ways.

exits.label: back upward to the dark that teaches itself to read
deeper into the palimpsest where old languages teach themselves to forget
toward the root-source where the first name was never named
